name: Alto del León (south side), Guadarrama
story: The Guadarrama pass, renamed Alto de los Leones by the victors, was one of the first battlefields of the war. Columns sent by General Mola from Valladolid and Segovia seized it on 22 July 1936 and held it against militia columns from Madrid in bloody fighting over the following days. The front then settled along the crest. Nationalist positions pushed south of the pass towards La Jarosa, the most advanced in the central sector, while Republican lines faced them on the lower slopes. Both sides fortified the mountain with concrete bunkers, shelters and observation posts that survive in the pine woods.
see: A bunker behind the roadside restaurant at the pass, an armoured observation post, and trenches, nests and a vaulted command bunker in the woods towards the La Jarosa reservoir.
plan: A 13 km circular walk links the positions (about 600 m of climbing). Mountain weather: carry warm clothing even in summer. The north side of the pass is in Segovia (see Castile).
